_exec_summary.SummaryText:
This is an executive summary of the policies, procedures, and activities for compliance with the EPA's Accidental Release Prevention Requirements - Risk Management Program pursuant to Title 40 Part 68 of the Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR 68) for Waste Managements Orchard Hills RNG facility at Davis Junction, IL.

The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source [40 CFR 68.155(a)]:
Waste Management is strongly committed to employee, public and environmental safety. This commitment is demonstrated by our comprehensive accidental release prevention program that encompasses design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training. Robust engineering controls are in place to prevent possible releases of regulated substances. The Orchard Hills RNG plant is a non-responding facility for releases of the RMP-listed chemicals, so the site utilizes an Emergency Action Plan.

The stationary source and regulated substances handled [40 CFR 68.155(b)]:
The Orchard Hills RNG facility converts landfill gas into renewable natural gas (RNG). Landfill gas from the wellfield enters the facility and undergoes several treatment steps, including hydrogen sulfide (H?S) removal and gas compression. The processed gas is then injected into a pipeline for distribution. The RMP regulated chemical in this facility is methane and the largest quantity of it is stored in the NRU (Nitrogen Rejection Unit) feed tank.

The general accidental release prevention program and chemical-specific prevention steps [40 CFR 68.155(c)]:
Waste Managements Orchard Hills RNG plant is not required to implement the Program Level 3 prevention program requirements under the RMP regulations because they are eligible for RMP Program Level 1. However, the facility is required to comply with the requirements for preventing or minimizing the consequences of catastrophic releases of flammable or explosive chemicals codified under the Process Safety Manage

ment (PSM) regulations (29 CFR 1910.119). The required elements of the PSM program relevant to general accidental release prevention are listed below:
-	Employee Participation
-	Process Safety Information
-	Process Hazard Analysis
-	Operating Procedures
-	Contractors
-	Pre-startup Safety Review
-	Mechanical Integrity
-	Hot Work Permit
-	Management of Change
-	Incident Investigation
-	Emergency Planning and Response
-	Compliance Audits
-	Trade Secrets
Orchard Hills RNG has a program in place to comply with these items and their specific requirements.

The five-year accident history [40 CFR 68.155(d)]:
This is a new facility, thus there have been no RMP-reportable accidents within the last five (5) years.

The emergency response program [40 CFR 68.155(e)]:
In the event of an incident, Orchard Hills RNG has systems in place to respond quickly. Processes can be shut down on an emergency basis and the facility has a plan in place for evacuations, adequate first aid, and medical treatment and notification of local emergency response agencies. The facility is a non-responding facility, and relies on the Davis Junction Fire Department to respond to chemical releases.

Planned changes to improve safety [40 CFR 68.155(f)]:
Orchard Hills RNG plant has several efforts in progress to improve safety and their prevention program. This includes a better system to track open action items that stem from PHAs, MOCs, and other prevention programs.

Waste Managements Orchard Hills RNG plant has completed this report to provide the public with information about our activities at this facility. We believe that the many controls instituted to maintain a safe operation, and our commitment to continuous improvement that an incident affecting our employees or the surrounding area is unlikely to occur.
